facts.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and duplex stainless steel 2205 were compared after three rapid heating-and-quenching cycles to approximately 1100 °C.
The alloys were tested by immersed reciprocating ball-on-flat tribo-corrosion against a 6.35 mm alumina ball while load was varied from 5 to 15 N and frequency from 3 to 9 Hz.
Tribo-corrosion tests were performed in 100 mL of deionized water at 25, 50, and 100 °C using a 3.5 mm stroke.
Each test used 3600 s of open-circuit-potential stabilization, 1800 s of sliding, and 300 s of post-sliding immersion to monitor repassivation.
The principal temperature comparison was conducted at 5 N and 5 Hz, with the 100 °C tests using a covered cell and reflux condenser.
Near 50 °C, accelerated passive-film repair without extensive brittle-film disruption produced a low-shear polishing regime that minimized wear.
At 100 °C, repeated formation, fracture, and removal of discontinuous oxide or tribo-layer patches caused oxidative or debris-assisted wear and greater friction instability.
The HEA's retained fine L12/B2 lamellar structure and comparatively homogeneous chromium availability supported more robust passive-film repair than in DS2205.
Across the tested temperatures, loads, and frequencies, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 had lower friction and approximately one-order-of-magnitude lower, more stable wear rates than DS2205.
After thermal shock, the HEA changed from 71% to 69% L12 and from 29% to 31% B2, corresponding to only about 2% phase transformation.
After identical thermal shock, DS2205 changed from 52% to 17% austenite and from 48% to 83% ferrite, a roughly 35-percentage-point γ-to-δ redistribution.
For both alloys, wear-volume loss followed 50 °C < 25 °C < 100 °C, so degradation was minimized near 50 °C rather than at room temperature or 100 °C.
